items.title: Introducing 224 Ventures
items.summary: Today I'm excited to introduce @224ventureshq, a deeply technical and GTM-focused venture firm investing in AI-native teams. We're launching with $100 million in assets under management.

items.title: Yann LeCun’s second attempt at a VC fund lands with $100M and Gemini’s co-lead as a partner
items.summary: 224 Ventures launches with more than $100 million in assets under management. Oriol Vinyals, who left DeepMind today to co-found Discovery Loop, joins as a partner alongside AIX Ventures co-founder Shaun Johnson.

items.title: Yann LeCun joins new VC firm backed by 244 LPs
items.summary: Former Meta chief scientist Yann LeCun has joined new firm 224 Ventures, which will invest in AI startups. 224 Ventures will be run by LeCun, alongside Google DeepMind researcher Oriol Vinyals and AIX Ventures founder Shaun Johnson.

items.title: LLM Detractors Pivot To “Pure LLM” Term After Recent LLM Breakthroughs
items.summary: Gary Marcus and former Meta Chief Scientist Yann LeCun have said that they had been talking about a “pure LLM” when they were talking about the limitations of the technology.

items.title: Noa Khamallah was a street kid and convict. Now his $10 million fund is taking on mega-VCs
items.summary: Noa Khamallah grew up without a microwave or a car, dropped out of school, and did time in prison before he ever wrote a check to a startup. When he wanted access to Yann LeCun, the researcher widely credited as the godfather of modern AI, he skipped the warm intro and cold-emailed him instead, subject line: “former convict, street kid, turned IPO, turned VC.” LeCun replied within hours: “You are a statistical anomaly. Welcome in.”

newItems.title: Self-supervised DXA representations encode multi-system disease risk, biological aging and heritability
newItems.tldr: It is shown that self-supervised learning (SSL) can convert raw DXA images into representations of systemic health, and prognostic information in DXA images that conventional readouts discard is revealed, learnable with relatively little data and modest compute.
newItems.abstract: Whole-body dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) scans are routinely acquired to measure bone density and regional body composition, leaving their spatial structure largely unused. Here, we show that self-supervised learning (SSL) can convert raw DXA images into representations of systemic health. We introduce LeDXA, a vision model based on a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) that learns by predicting latent representations rather than reconstructing pixels. newItems.title: HP-JEPA: Hierarchical Partitioning for Multi-Resolution Graph Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning
newItems.tldr: Horsepower-JEPA organizes each graph into an ordered bank of coarse-to-fine partition resolutions and performs context-target latent prediction separately at each resolution using an online encoder, an exponential-moving-average target encoder, and a latent predictor.
newItems.abstract: Graph self-supervised learning aims to learn transferable representations from large-scale unlabeled graph data. Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) avoid explicit negative-pair construction and raw-input reconstruction by predicting masked targets directly in latent space. However, existing graph JEPAs typically rely on a single predefined graph partition, biasing the learned representations toward one structural granularity and limiting their ability to capture complementary patterns at different graph scales. newItems.title: Unpacking Open Source Artificial Intelligence: Toward a Framework for Openness in Foundation Models
newItems.tldr: A framework for analyzing openness across the AI stack is proposed, reviewing prior approaches and highlighting the diverse motivations for pursuing openness, showing how these map onto different forms of openness at both the model and system levels.
newItems.abstract: There has been a robust debate about the benefits and risks of “open sourcing” foundation models. Yet much of the discourse has lacked specificity, either remaining overly abstract or focusing narrowly on a limited set of technical components. This is partly because defining open source for foundation models is challenging, given their significant differences from traditional software development. newItems.title: Music-JEPA: Learning a World Model of Sound from Action
newItems.tldr: This work proposes to learn a world model of piano sound using JEPA by framing music as an action-conditioned system, and shows that the learned model captures the relationships between musical actions and their resulting sound.
newItems.abstract: Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) have recently emerged as a paradigm for learning world models by predicting latent representations, offering a promising direction for self-supervised learning. While initial attempts have applied JEPA to the music domain, it remains unclear how such frameworks can naturally support the formation of a world model for music. In this work, we propose to learn a world model of piano sound using JEPA by framing music as an action-conditioned system: the audio is treated as the state, and the pianoroll as the instrument action. newItems.title: Patch Policy: Efficient Embodied Control via Dense Visual Representations
newItems.tldr: This work believes Patch Policy provides a pipeline for the robotics community to readily leverage continuing progress in visual representation learning, without sacrificing the training efficiency or inference speed required for high-frequency, reactive control.
newItems.abstract: Pretrained dense visual features from Vision Transformers (ViTs) are powerful yet have been underutilized in robot learning. Modern robot policies either compress each observation into a single global token, or rely on visual backbones trained from scratch, sacrificing both fine-grained spatial detail and the benefits of large-scale visual pre-training. newItems.title: AdaJEPA: An Adaptive Latent World Model
newItems.tldr: AdaJEPA is an adaptive latent world model that performs test-time adaptation within the closed loop of model predictive control (MPC), and substantially improves planning success with as few as one gradient step per MPC replanning step.
newItems.abstract: Latent world models enable planning from high-dimensional observations by predicting future states in a compact latent space. However, these models are typically kept frozen at test time: when their predictions become inaccurate, planning can fail, especially under test-time distribution shift. To address this, we propose AdaJEPA, an adaptive latent world model that performs test-time adaptation within the closed loop of model predictive control (MPC). newItems.title: SkyJEPA: Learning Long-Horizon World Models for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Control of Quadrotors
newItems.tldr: The JEPA-style model for real-time quadrotor control is introduced, which combines a latent dynamics model with a novel physics-inspired prober that maps frozen latents to interpretable state, enabling physically grounded long-horizon prediction.
newItems.abstract: Accurate dynamics models are critical for informed decision-making in robotic systems, particularly for agile aerial vehicles operating under uncertainty. Neural network dynamics models are attractive for capturing complex nonlinear effects, but existing predictive approaches struggle with long-horizon forecasting because their autoregressive rollout mechanism amplifies errors over time. newItems.title: S-JEPA : Soft Clustering Anchors for Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning
newItems.tldr: S-JEPA is introduced, a JEPA-style encoder-predictor pair trained to match the soft posteriors of a Gaussian Mixture Model at masked positions via KL divergence, establishing a new Pareto frontier without offline re-clustering or teacher distillation.

newItems.title: You Don't Need Strong Assumptions: Visual Representation Learning via Temporal Differences
newItems.tldr: Temporal Difference in Vision (TDV) is introduced, a new paradigm for self-supervised learning from video that avoids existing inductive biases, relying instead on a causal assumption that the past causes the future.
newItems.abstract: Progress in AI has largely been driven by methods that assume less. headline: LeCun bets on the ecosystem, not just the lab with launch of 224 Ventures
stateOfPlay: The defining event of this week for AMI's orbit is Yann LeCun's big formal step as a venture capitalist. The launch of 224 Ventures, a $100 million fund co-founded with AIX Ventures' Shaun Johnson and the newly minted Oriol Vinyals (who departed DeepMind this week to co-found Discovery Loop), raises LeCun's profile as an ecosystem builder. It's important to note that LeCun is already an active Business Angel and has additional VC affiliations. Still, read alongside a steady drumbeat of JEPA-variant papers bearing his name, the move suggests someone who is expanding his architectural bets.

threads.title: 224 Ventures is LeCun staking a claim on the post-LLM investment landscape
threads.narrative:
224 Ventures opens with $100 million in assets under management and a stated focus on 'deeply technical and GTM-focused' AI-native teams. The name itself — 224 — is a nod to the number of neurons in a specific early neural network layer, a piece of branding that signals the fund intends to wear its technical credentials conspicuously.

Vinyals left DeepMind on the same day the fund was announced, joining 224 Ventures as a partner and co-founding his own new venture, Discovery Loop. That dual role, combined with LeCun's parallel involvement with AMI, suggests 224 Ventures is conceived less as a full-time operating firm and more as a network node, a vehicle through which a cluster of senior researchers can back and advise the next generation of non-LLM AI startups. For AMI, the implication is worth watching: LeCun's credibility and deal flow are now formally attached to an external vehicle, which could funnel aligned companies and researchers into AMI's orbit, or simply compete for his attention.

evidence.label: The Next Web — LeCun's VC fund with Vinyals

threads.title: Three hires in three cities reveal an infrastructure and multimodal agenda beneath the world-model rhetoric
threads.narrative:
There were several hiring signals we surfaced. Amir Bar, an assistant professor at Imperial College London and a former Meta researcher, brings serious computer vision and multimodal credentials to AMI's London footprint. Ayaan Naveed Malik, a recent Stanford graduate joining in New York, arrives with a background in robotics and multimodal AI, exactly the domains where JEPA-style world models need to prove themselves. Together they suggest AMI is assembling the technical bench to move from theory to working systems.

The third hire is Haoyi Li, who is joining in Singapore. He is not a machine-learning researcher, but rather a large-scale developer infrastructure engineer known for work at Databricks and Dropbox, and the author of the Mill build tool. His GitHub activity this week — closing issues in his own `com-lihaoyi/mill` repo and commenting on a Scala 3 pull request — confirms he is already active on infrastructure concerns. Hiring someone of Li's profile at this stage signals that AMI is taking the underlying engineering platform seriously, not just the research layer above it.

threads.title: JEPA proliferates across domains. The architecture is becoming a platform
threads.narrative:
Administrative note: We revamped the backend in terms of the way publications of AMI team members are captured, so the filter is more comprehensive. That means we digested 444 new items (woof!) attributed to the team since the last window. But the directional signal is hard to miss: JEPA-style architectures are spreading into domains far beyond the vision tasks where they originated. Among the newly surfaced papers bearing LeCun's name: LeDXA applies a joint-embedding predictive architecture to whole-body DXA medical scans, learning representations of systemic health from just 11,540 unlabeled scans with 'relatively little data and modest compute.' HP-JEPA extends the paradigm to graph-structured data, using hierarchical multi-resolution partitioning to overcome the single-granularity limitation of prior graph JEPAs. Music-JEPA frames piano sound as an action-conditioned world model. SkyJEPA applies it to quadrotor drone control for zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. AdaJEPA adds test-time adaptation inside a model-predictive-control loop.

Taken together, these papers — spanning medical imaging, graphs, audio, and robotics — are less a scatter of independent projects and more a coordinated demonstration that JEPA is a general-purpose representational substrate. LeDXA is particularly notable because it is the first paper in this cluster to demonstrate the paradigm working on clinical data with real health outcomes, thereby broadening the argument for JEPA well beyond the AI research community. Whether LeCun is the intellectual originator of each paper or a senior author lending imprimatur, the cumulative effect is the same: JEPA is being positioned as a platform, not a paper.

evidence.label: LeDXA — JEPA for medical DXA imaging
Music-JEPA — world model of piano sound

threads.title: A talent-sourcing hire and newly surfaced investors signal AMI is preparing for a larger recruiting push
threads.narrative: The one new recent job posting is not a researcher or engineer: it is a Talent Intelligence & Sourcing Partner, based in Paris, sitting inside General and Administration. Hiring dedicated recruiting infrastructure at this stage is a forward-looking signal. A new in-house recruiter suggests AMI's leadership expects the headcount curve to steepen materially in the months ahead.

threads.title: Brian Li's agentic evaluation work points to an emerging benchmark priority
threads.narrative:
The most technically specific GitHub signal comes from Brian Li, who contributed the majority of AMI-attributable commits. His activity in `EvolvingLMMs-Lab/lmms-eval` is notable for what he named the branches: `brian/feat/agentic-env-interface` and `brian/feat/agentic-game-minimal`. These are not incremental patches; they suggest Li is building out evaluation infrastructure for agentic, interactive environments within a multimodal LLM benchmark framework. That work sits at the intersection of evaluation methodology and the kind of embodied, action-taking AI that world-model approaches are meant to enable.

This is a thin signal — branch names and pull requests, not published results — but it is directionally consistent with the rest of the week's picture. If AMI's research agenda centers on world models and embodied agents, having team members actively developing the evaluation tooling for agentic multimodal systems is exactly the kind of preparatory infrastructure work you would expect to see.

evidence.label: Brian Li — agentic env interface branch

evidence.title: The 'pure LLM' reframe is a rhetorical repositioning, not a retreat
evidence.narrative:
A brief but telling news item this week: OfficeChai reported that LeCun and Gary Marcus have begun distinguishing between 'LLMs' and 'pure LLMs' when discussing architectural limitations, after recent LLM capability gains attracted criticism of their earlier skepticism. This is a subtle but meaningful move. Rather than conceding the argument, the reframe carves out a narrower target — the 'pure' autoregressive text predictor — while leaving room to argue that systems augmented with world models, planning, or other non-LLM components are a different and more defensible category.

For AMI, this matters because LeCun's public credibility as the alternative-to-LLMs voice is part of the company's implicit positioning. If the framing holds, it preserves the intellectual case for JEPA-based architectures even as LLM benchmarks continue to improve. It also maps cleanly onto 224 Ventures' stated thesis of backing 'AI-native teams' — which, read charitably, means teams building beyond the pure-LLM paradigm.

evidence.label: OfficeChai — LeCun and Marcus on 'pure LLM'
Open Source AI framework — Communications of the ACM

signals.text: David Fan's paper on multimodal pretraining derives 'efficient pretraining recipes that achieve strong generative performance using only 5% of the compute budget' — a compute-efficiency framing that fits naturally with the resource constraints of a startup lab rather than a hyperscaler.

AMI board member Pascale Fung publicly called on NVIDIA to expand free or subsidized compute for academic researchers — a pointed reminder that even well-funded AI startups outside the hyperscaler tier face GPU access as a structural constraint.

AMI's intern cohort across Paris and New York was quietly reported this week. Building a bench through internships at this stage is consistent with the university-pipeline cultivation visible in LeCun's academic speaking circuit.

threads.whatToWatch: With a dedicated talent-sourcing hire now in place and seven additional seed investors surfaced, the structural conditions for an accelerated hiring wave are present — watch whether the open-role count grows sharply over the next month. On the research side, Brian Li's agentic evaluation branches in lmms-eval are worth tracking: if those PRs merge and expand, they may foreshadow AMI's first public benchmark contributions in the agentic multimodal space.
